results.title: Every depended-on CLI flag exists
results.claim: All 33 flags the architecture depends on are present in the installed CLI, with the semantics the plan assumes.
results.failureImpact: A missing flag invalidates whichever mechanism depends on it and may force the PTY contingency for that capability.
results.detail: All 33 required flags present AND declared in the option column (69 flags parsed).

results.title: --bare would break subscription auth (so it must never be used)
results.claim: The installed binary documents that --bare reads auth strictly from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/apiKeyHelper and never from OAuth or the keychain.
results.failureImpact: If the semantics differ, the prohibition in CLAUDE.md §3 rests on a stale quote and must be re-derived.
results.detail: Help text confirms API-key-only auth under --bare, verbatim as the plan quotes it.

results.title: --safe-mode disables the customizations Guidelane depends on
results.claim: --safe-mode disables plugins, hooks, skills, and MCP servers.
results.failureImpact: If it were harmless, the prohibition would be unnecessary noise in the constitution.
results.detail: --safe-mode help mentions disabling: skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers.

results.title: `claude doctor` exists and can back G0
results.claim: The CLI ships an environment health check that Guidelane can wrap instead of reimplementing preflight.
results.failureImpact: G0 must implement all environment checks itself.
results.detail: Subcommand present; G0 should wrap it rather than duplicate environment checks.

results.title: `claude plugin validate --strict` and `plugin eval` exist
results.claim: The behaviour pack can be regression-tested by the vendor tooling rather than by vibes.
results.failureImpact: S4 loses its objective gate; jargon-leak checking stays manual.
results.detail: plugin subcommands — validate: true, eval: true.

results.title: The fixture plugin passes `plugin validate --strict`
results.claim: A plugin laid out the way Guidelane will ship its behaviour pack validates strictly — manifest fields, component locations, hook schema.
results.failureImpact: The plugin layout in the plan is wrong and the behaviour pack would fail to load in front of users.
results.detail: Fixture plugin validates strictly (manifest + skills + agents + hooks + bundled MCP).

results.title: A timed-out child takes its whole process tree with it
results.claim: When the harness times out a child, the process-group kill reaps its grandchildren too — so a stuck engine session cannot leave an authenticated `claude`, a stdio MCP server, or a Bash grandchild running against the user's quota.
results.failureImpact: Orphaned engine processes keep spending a friend's subscription after a crash, with nobody reading their output. This is the S2 exit gate's core question, and it is invisible to every happy-path probe.
results.detail: Timeout killed the whole group: the direct child AND its grandchild were both gone afterwards. The process-group kill added at S0 close does what it claims.

results.title: A grandchild that escapes the process group cannot hang the suite
results.claim: When a grandchild in its own process group holds the stdout pipe open, the child's 'close' event never fires — and the settle watchdog resolves the call anyway, so the run continues instead of hanging forever.
results.failureImpact: The single worst outcome the product can have: a run that stops with no output, no error, and no terminal event. In the nightly job it burns to the CI cap; in front of a non-coder it is "the computer froze".
results.detail: Escaped grandchild held the pipe open and 'close' never came, yet the call settled in 8006ms via the watchdog. A stuck session degrades into evidence instead of a silent hang. As designed, the escapee outlived the group kill — the probe reaped it itself.

results.title: The exercised CLI version is inside the tested range
results.claim: Every run states the engine version it exercised and refuses to present its results as conformance evidence when that version is outside the range the suite has actually been validated against.
results.failureImpact: REVIEW-01 #5's remedy is a tested version range plus a nightly probe. CI pins the version; the local launchd run does not, so an auto-update could silently move the engine under a green report and nobody would notice.
results.detail: Engine 2.1.220 is inside the tested range 2.1.220–2.1.999.

results.title: system/init is a machine-checkable receipt of the whole context package
results.claim: The first stream event enumerates what the session actually got — tools, mcp_servers (with status), plugins, skills, agents, model, permissionMode, apiKeySource, memory_paths, version — so the orchestrator can assert its context package arrived instead of hoping.
results.failureImpact: A stage can run to completion with Atlas silently absent, on a stale CLI, or with the wrong permission mode, and the bad output gets attributed to the model rather than to a broken context package.
results.detail: init carries every field the orchestrator needs to assert on, and apiKeySource is ASSERTED (=none, the auth-mode discriminator) rather than merely recorded. version=2.1.220.

results.title: A spawned session inherits the operator's whole configuration unless isolated
results.claim: Isolation requires BOTH --strict-mcp-config AND --setting-sources "". With MCP isolation alone, the child still inherits the operator's plugins, skills, agents and permission mode.
results.failureImpact: Fresh-session-per-stage stops meaning reproducible context: a friend's own skills, hooks and permission defaults silently alter Guidelane runs, and the owner's personal constitution is injected into every build session. Drift control — the point of the architecture — quietly evaporates.
results.detail: --strict-mcp-config alone LEAKS operator config (plugins 4, skills 24, agents 10, permissionMode bypassPermissions); adding --setting-sources "" reduces it to exactly the CLI's built-in floor (16 skills, 5 agents, 0 plugins, 0 mcp_servers, permissionMode default). Both flags required — and the floor is NOT empty, so stage allow-lists must withhold Task/Skill unless a stage deliberately needs them (ADR-008 amendment).

results.title: A MessageDisplay hook rewrite reaches stream-json, not just the terminal
results.claim: A MessageDisplay hook returning displayContent replaces the assistant text that Guidelane reads from --output-format stream-json. Guidelane never renders the terminal, so a terminal-only rewrite would give the product exactly zero protection.
results.failureImpact: R3 mechanism 4 disappears from the product surface and jargon suppression falls entirely to the cockpit's whitelist renderer.
results.detail: Rewrite propagated into assistant text AND the terminal result — mechanism 4 is real on the product surface. Note: hook failure is fail-open (the engine emits the original text), so the cockpit renderer stays the guarantee.

results.title: Bidirectional stream-json round-trip with partial messages and replay
results.claim: The engine accepts stream-json on stdin and emits a parseable stream-json event sequence including a terminal result event, partial message deltas, and replayed user messages.
results.failureImpact: The cockpit cannot render a live activity feed; the entire event-translation layer (R3 mechanism 3) has no input.
results.detail: Full round-trip. Event types: system, user, stream_event, rate_limit_event, assistant, result.

results.title: The result event carries usage and cost data
results.claim: The terminal result event exposes token usage (and, where applicable, cost) so the per-run cost line and token telemetry have a real source.
results.failureImpact: Token economy becomes unmeasurable — the R13 workstream loses its instrument and crew routing can never be tuned by data.
results.detail: Result keys: is_error, duration_api_ms, num_turns, stop_reason, session_id, total_cost_usd, usage, modelUsage, permission_denials, terminal_reason, fast_mode_state, fast_mode_disabled_reason, subtype, api_error_status, result, ttft_ms, ttft_stream_ms, time_to_request_ms, type, duration_ms, uuid. usage=true, cost field=total_cost_usd.

results.title: --json-schema forces schema-valid structured output
results.claim: Passing a JSON Schema constrains the response to valid, parseable JSON matching that schema — the mechanism behind schema-valid blueprints, plans, and review verdicts.
results.failureImpact: G1/G2/G5 artifacts lose their protocol-level guarantee and the orchestrator must hand-parse model prose — the single largest source of pipeline fragility.
results.detail: Structured output matched the schema, including the nested acceptance-criteria array.

results.title: --append-system-prompt reaches the model, and --tools "" removes the toolset
results.claim: Per-session persona injection takes effect, and the built-in toolset can be emptied — the two cheapest levers behind the non-engineer surface and per-stage tool scoping.
results.failureImpact: R3 mechanism 1 and the per-stage tool scoping in RESEARCH-02 §5 both fail; review sessions could not be made read-only by construction.
results.detail: Appended system prompt changed behaviour in a headless session.

results.title: --agents defines a dispatchable agent inline
results.claim: Role agents can be injected per session as JSON without shipping files. NOTE: not load-bearing — Guidelane runs each review lens as its own top-level session (ADR-002), so subagent dispatch is a convenience, not a dependency.
results.failureImpact: None structural. Lenses ship as plugin agents (proven by p-plugin-skill-headless) or as separate sessions, which is the actual design.
results.detail: `--agents` registers inline: the init receipt lists probe_lens beside the 5 built-ins. Dispatch observed: no (not asserted — whether the model elects to call Task is model behaviour, not engine capability).

results.title: --max-budget-usd behaviour under the operator's current auth
results.claim: REVIEW-01 argued the flag is inert under subscription auth. This probe settles whether it is enforced, accepted-but-inert, or rejected.
results.failureImpact: If inert, the guardrail story for subscription users must rest entirely on timeouts, cycle caps, and retry ceilings — and RESEARCH-01 §4.1 stays corrected.
results.detail: --max-budget-usd 0.0000001 → enforced (call refused or halted by the budget ceiling). Exit 1.

evidence.verdict: enforced (call refused or halted by the budget ceiling)

results.title: Effort, model, and fallback-model compose in one invocation
results.claim: Crew routing can set model and effort per session, with a fallback chain, in a single command.
results.failureImpact: ADR-004 crew routing cannot be expressed per stage; token economy loses its largest lever.
results.detail: Accepted together; model reported as not surfaced in result.

results.title: Headless permissions are fail-closed: auto denies, auto + allow-list permits
results.claim: In a headless session, --permission-mode auto ALONE denies tool calls (no interactive grant is possible), while auto plus an explicit --allowedTools list permits exactly the listed tools. This makes the engine itself the fail-closed layer and per-stage tool scoping the primary safety mechanism.
results.failureImpact: If auto alone permitted everything, safety would rest solely on our PreToolUse hook. If the allow-list did not work either, no autonomous stage could touch the filesystem at all and the pipeline could not build anything.
results.detail: auto alone: DENIED the write (fail-closed, exit 0). Structural denial channels observed: tool_result.is_error. The model still claimed success — a live example of the state-hallucination failure the pipeline exists to catch. auto + --allowedTools Write: wrote the file.

results.title: Session id, resume, and fork behave as the artifact store assumes
results.claim: A caller-supplied session id is honoured, the session can be resumed with continuity, and --fork-session branches instead of mutating.
results.failureImpact: The session-reuse economy mode and phase continuation both break; kill-9 resumability must rely on artifacts alone.
results.detail: Session id honoured, resume kept context, fork produced a new id.

results.title: Atlas-shaped MCP server loads via --mcp-config with --strict-mcp-config isolation
results.claim: A local stdio MCP server passed on the command line is reachable in a headless session, its tool is callable, and --strict-mcp-config keeps the operator's own MCP servers out.
results.failureImpact: Atlas cannot be delivered to sessions the way ADR-003 specifies, and a friend's own MCP config could leak into Guidelane runs.
results.detail: MCP server loaded from the command line and its tool was callable under a fail-closed allow-list (mcp__<server>__<tool>).

results.title: A session-only plugin loads and its skill is invocable in -p mode
results.claim: --plugin-dir loads a plugin for one session with no marketplace or install step, and its skills resolve in headless mode.
results.failureImpact: The behaviour pack cannot be delivered per session; the dual-surface strategy and every persona/guard mechanism lose their carrier.
results.detail: Session-only plugin loaded and its skill resolved from a headless prompt.

results.title: Which hook lifecycle events actually fire in a headless session
results.claim: The events the non-engineer surface depends on — MessageDisplay, PermissionRequest, PreToolUse, Stop, Notification — fire in `claude -p`, not only in interactive sessions. Additionally, a MessageDisplay hook that writes nothing to stdout must not suppress assistant text.
results.failureImpact: If MessageDisplay/PermissionRequest are interactive-only, R3 mechanism 4 disappears and the cockpit's deterministic rendering floor becomes the ONLY defence — a plan change, not a tuning issue. If empty-stdout MessageDisplay blanks output, the hook is unusable as written.
results.detail: Fired: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, MessageDisplay, Stop, SessionEnd | Assistant marker survived the MessageDisplay hook (empty stdout = no suppression). | Hook events in stream: 12

results.title: A plugin-bundled MCP server loads, and its tools carry the plugin-scoped name
results.claim: An .mcp.json inside the plugin root resolves ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, its tool is reachable, and the exact tool name is discoverable — the allow-list cannot be written without knowing that name.
results.failureImpact: Atlas must be passed via --mcp-config on every invocation instead of riding along with the behaviour pack; and a wrong allow-list name silently disables Atlas in every session.
results.detail: Bundled server registers and its tool round-trips as `mcp__plugin_guidelane-probe_echo__guidelane_probe_echo`; status at init was `connected` (races the handshake — do not gate on it). --strict-mcp-config excludes plugin-bundled servers entirely (mcp_servers empty): isolation and plugin-bundled delivery are mutually exclusive, so Atlas must ship via --mcp-config (ADR-003 corrected).

results.title: Engine version is machine-readable for the tested-range check
results.claim: Guidelane can read the CLI version programmatically to enforce a tested-version range.
results.failureImpact: Version governance (REVIEW-01 #5) has no input; breakage is discovered by users.
results.detail: Parsed version 2.1.220 from `claude --version`.

results.title: Auth mode is inspectable without exposing a credential
results.claim: Guidelane can tell whether the operator is on subscription auth or an API key — needed to explain budget-flag behaviour and to route the right guardrail story — without ever reading the credential itself.
results.failureImpact: The product cannot tailor guardrails or explain limits honestly; the budget-flag finding cannot be surfaced to the right users.
results.detail: auth status --json exposes loggedIn, authMethod, subscriptionType — mode is readable without touching a credential. 4 personal field(s) in the same payload must be projected away (ADR-008).

results.title: What `--permission-mode auto` means is the same on every machine
results.claim: The auto-mode classifier (allow / soft_deny / hard_deny rules) on this machine is the shipped default, so ADR-007's "auto + explicit allow-list" contract means the same thing on a friend's laptop as on the owner's.
results.failureImpact: The classifier is per-machine user settings (`auto-mode reset` works by removing the autoMode section from user settings) and is admin-overridable. If it drifts, `auto` silently means something different per install and the permission contract is unportable.
results.detail: Effective classifier is byte-identical to the shipped defaults (allow:17, soft_deny:65, hard_deny:1, environment:20).

results.title: The spawned child's auto-updater can be governed
results.claim: An environment variable or setting disables the auto-updater in child sessions, so a mid-run update cannot change the engine under a running pipeline.
results.failureImpact: REVIEW-01 #5 has no remedy: every user's engine can change simultaneously, mid-project.
results.detail: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 is honoured and observable: "enabled" -> "disabled (set by env: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER)" (the engine names the env var as the source). The harness sets it on every child, so a mid-run update cannot change the engine under a running pipeline. REVIEW-01 #5 has its remedy.

results.title: The stream carries a structured rate-limit event with a reset timestamp
results.claim: Every stream-json session emits a `rate_limit_event` carrying at least a status, a window type, and a machine-readable reset time — so the Night Shift supervisor can pause precisely and resume at the window boundary instead of blind-polling.
results.failureImpact: Without it, unattended runs must guess: backoff-poll with capped attempts and a manual morning resume, and the morning report cannot say when capacity returns.
results.detail: rate_limit_event present — status=allowed, window=five_hour, resetsAt=1785469200 (epoch seconds — supervisor can sleep to the boundary).

evidence.note: Only the healthy ("allowed") branch is observed here; the rejected branch is not provoked on purpose.
